newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes up on U.S. unit's weakness.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes up on U.S. unit's weakness.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished higher on Wednesday as the U.S. dollar sank after the U.S. Federal Reserve Board left interest rates unchanged.

The rate ended at T$27.470 versus T$27.482 at Tuesday's close. Turnover was a US$239.5 million, slightly shy of Tuesday's US$241.5 million but remained one of the more active trading sessions in recent doldrums.

After a strong opening, the Taiwan dollar built on the overnight momentum to trade higher, with only a brief respite in late morning. More U.S. dollar selling emerged towards the close, pushing the Taiwan unit to finish at the day's peak.
The currency market had priced in a 25 basis point hike of the Fed funds rate. Without a rate rise, the American dollar's slide was widely expected, dealers said.
The Taiwan dollar benefited from disappointed liquidation by exporters, who had held dollars in anticipation of some quarter-end demand from importers, one dealer said.
"After the Fed decided not to raise rate, the dollar could weaken some more," said the dealer at a foreign bank. "So importers found it unnecessary to lock in the rates now."
A T$27.45-50 trading range was seen in the near term.
